description:

host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

In the other direction, a lovely greenway runs along Reeds Creek, or you can simply stroll around the eclectic neighborhood. host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. host_about:
When I am in the mountains I am home!  I've lived in the Piedmont region of NC for 14 years now but, Asheville will always be home.  I am on the struggle bus of being a mom to my two boys, Kelvin 4 and Brody 2. My night in shining armor, Ben loves coaching middle school football and teaching 8th grade math. 
I was raised by a single mother from Cleveland Ohio with strong beliefs and the loudest laugh in the south! She believed that the most important things in life are those that can never be taken away; education and experiences!  She is the fundamental reason I am a realist, yet fearless and ready to take on the world. Our yearly trips to NYC led to us sharing a love of the city and Broadway! 
In 2007 Ben surprised me for a weekend trip to NYC. His first trip of many and my most memorable; he proposed on top of the Empire State Building! See why I call him my night in shining armor?!?  Of course Ben caught the travel bug too and has been back to NYC countless times! He's expanded to international travel! Last year it was a trip to Jamaica that led to my mom and I talking ourselves into seeing Hamilton before the original cast split up! She ended up backing out but of course Ben knows the number one mom lesson, "You don't regret what you do, only what you don't do." It was a priceless experience I wouldn't trade! 
I am proud to say my boys can tell you all about their trips to New York City(while singing Hamilton), New England and all the way down to Key West! Live your life, enjoy it,cars are designed to be driven, money is made to be spent - go make lasting memories!

coffee
massages
doing anything and everything outdoors

host_about:
Early exposure to the Blue Ridge Mountains and a love of cycling initially drew me to Asheville. The artistic diversity of the community reawakened my interest in architecture and fed a desire to contribute to Asheville's thriving downtown. 
	
Built in 1924, 59 Broadway came on the market in 2013 and was unusual in that it had only served as warehouse space with consequently very little infrastructure, thus providing a clean canvas for my modernist vision. Having sat empty for a decade, it was in remarkably great shape. But most importantly, it had SOUL.

After a year of planning, a project incorporating the interplay of natural, urban, and personal environments with attention to space, lighting, quality, and simplicity was begun. Twelve-foot ceilings, original hardwood flooring, simple layout, and uncluttered space help imbue the feeling of warmth and calm that initially drew me in. Unlike any other historic building downtown, it’s newly engineered windows all along the northern wall provide an abundance of natural light further enhancing the unique ambiance.

My wife Constance and I, along with the seasoned guidance of an interior designer, picked furnishings that we would want in our own home, including art and ceramics throughout made by local artists who are also our friends. host_about:
Early exposure to the Blue Ridge Mountains and a love of cycling initially drew me to Asheville. The artistic diversity of the community reawakened my interest in architecture and fed a desire to contribute to Asheville's thriving downtown. 
	
Built in 1924, 59 Broadway came on the market in 2013 and was unusual in that it had only served as warehouse space with consequently very little infrastructure, thus providing a clean canvas for my modernist vision. Having sat empty for a decade, it was in remarkably great shape. But most importantly, it had SOUL.

After a year of planning, a project incorporating the interplay of natural, urban, and personal environments with attention to space, lighting, quality, and simplicity was begun. Twelve-foot ceilings, original hardwood flooring, simple layout, and uncluttered space help imbue the feeling of warmth and calm that initially drew me in. Unlike any other historic building downtown, it’s newly engineered windows all along the northern wall provide an abundance of natural light further enhancing the unique ambiance.

My wife Constance and I, along with the seasoned guidance of an interior designer, picked furnishings that we would want in our own home, including art and ceramics throughout made by local artists who are also our friends. We especially love the bird’s eye view of the city’s comings and goings while perched on the full length window seats. Mesmerizing.

neighborhood_overview: Things have really come alive in West Asheville since I bought my home in 2000'. It's been amazing to be a part of my neighborhood and community becoming more diverse and eclectic. Most of the homes in this area like mine date back to the late 1920's.
host_about:
I love to travel and soak up as much local culture as I can wherever I go, so I decided to share my home with people like you that share this passion. 
  I grew up in Atlanta and discovered Asheville by way of Maui. I  lived on Maui and Kauai for a few years and when it came time to move back closer to family a Maui  friend suggested Asheville as an alternative to the big city.  He’d grown up in Chapel Hill and in Asheville. 
 So, after enough culture shock back in Atlanta I decided to explore Asheville in the late 90’s. After being here for a week or so wuth my Boxer Buddy I knew I'd found our new home.  I'd also developed a love of old houses growing up in Atlanta so bought this 1927 bungalow from a friend in 2000. 
 In 2006 I decided to create a new space with a view. Only by cleaning my gutters did I notice what a great view to the west there was from a slightly higher perspective. So, I designed and built the “Treetop Loft” and lived up there for many years and rented the downstairs long term. I now love sharing this space and hearing  feedback I get about the design, the light and feel of the space.
 I'm also artist and one of the reasons I moved back downstairs is to have more wall space for the larger paintings I'd missed. 
 I’m an avid motorcyclist, lover of the outdoors and great beer so Asheville has been the perfect home for a long time now! 

  I do hope you enjoy Asheville as much as I do !

neighborhood_overview:
LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Unit 201 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados alike.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

We say, when you go to Asheville, this is where you want to be. Right here, in the heart of Asheville. Right here, on N. Lexington Ave., in a building once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.

The space
Right here, in Apartment 202 at 80 LEX: in an ultra-sleek, über-chic 1-bedroom, 1-bathroom apartment that epitomizes the heart, soul and spirit of trendy Asheville.

Because here, in 566 square-feet of industrial loft space, exposed brick, pops of color, and layered textures, Apartment 202 offers an only-in-Asheville kind of retreat: handpicked décor and vintage furnishings, curated artwork and upholstered barn doors.

A home-away-from-home that is both on trend and yet, thoroughly wel
neighborhood_overview:
Location, Location, Location
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Apartment 202 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados alike.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

I have on-site classes and tours, and tiny home guests are welcome to take advantage of these opportunities upon advanced notice. I enjoy getting to know people from all walks of life. 

In my 20s, traveling was a big part of my life, and I was lucky to experience a lot of the country and explored a fair amount abroad as well. Australia, Cuba, Puerto Rico and the deserts of Utah (particularly Escalante) are some of my favorite memories. I also lived and worked at an eco-resort in St. John USVI for a half of a year. host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
“Travel changes you. As you move through this life and this world you change things slightly, you leave marks behind, however small. And in return, life—and travel—leaves marks on you.”  – Anthony Bourdain.

We LIVE to travel! Heather spent many years working in the airline industry which allowed us to see 40+ countries. The Anthony Bourdain show “No Reservations”  sums up our travel style. We tend to book the first night to recover from jet lag and then keep the rest of the trip open. We like to see where our travels want to take us. Seeking out the “undiscovered” places and truly connecting with locals is what we are all about. Some of our favorites: Luang Prabang / Bagan / Zanzibar / Bali / Colombia / Ronda (got engaged) / Samana, Dominican Republic (got married) / Chicago / Isla Holbox (shhhh, keep it a secret). Through many of these travels Airbnb has been a big piece of the puzzle.  

The two of us met in Aspen, CO. Heather is originally from Chicago and Mark from Virginia Beach. Although Heather loved city life her wanderlust brought her to Aspen for thirteen years.  Mark had been living in Washington D.C. doing the daily grind as an architect and had heard about a firm in Aspen that was hiring. He jumped on the chance and never looked back!  Aspen was a fantastic place to live and truly enjoy life. It taught us that you can live more simply and have a healthier quality of life. 

After a long stint out west and with a child on the way we decided it was time to be closer to family. We had a list of 30 towns all over the midwest and eastern U.S. which we either visited or did research on. After visiting Asheville we knew it was our next stop in life. Mark has opened his own office and Heather teaches at a creative arts center while studying interior design. Besides continuing to travel, we hike with our son and two dogs as often as possible and love checking out the awesome breweries and restaurants Asheville has to offer. We've also just begun hosting on Airbnb and really enjoy meeting fellow travelers and hosting them in our guest suite. 

We hope to inspire others to get out of their comfort zone and check out other places and people on this amazing planet! 

"Not until we are lost do we begin to understand ourselves." 
- Henry David Thoreau

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

If you are looking for a mountain experience but also close to town this is the place! We have plenty of relaxing space with an abundance of windows allowing for relaxing natural light and gorgeous views.
The recent addition of a large stone patio out front to enjoy the views is a spectacular way to unwind after a day of exploring.

The main floor has a foyer, 1/2 bath, kitchen, living space with two sided stone gas fireplace, and a dining room. There is a wrap around porch with outside dining, grill, fire pit, and roc

neighborhood_overview:
The house is in a convenient location to go any direction. host_about:

host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

I'm always available via phone or the app and am happy to answer any and all questions you have!

Best wishes, Christy

neighborhood_overview:
Come masquerade as a local and enjoy the short walk to the dozens of popular dining, music, shopping and people watching activities Haywood Rd. has to offer. Though quite close to downtown, 100 years ago West Asheville was its own town independent of Asheville. As a result, this unique area of town has its own “Mini-Downtown” that is centered around Haywood Rd. For the last few decades this commercial corridor has enjoyed a period of reinvestment by the community and area businesses. Several cool and unique restaurants, coffee shops, bars, bakeries, breweries and shops have chosen West Asheville as their home. Century old houses are being renovated back to life and new homes are being built on every available lot. As the historic town of “West Asheville” was never very big, the entire area is very walkable and there are lots of cool old buildings, churches, trees and houses.
The River Arts District and New Belgium Brewing are a 5 minute drive, Biltmore Estate is a 15 minute drive

name: Private Grove Park Suite near downtown Asheville!
description:
Located in the gorgeous, charming Grove Park neighborhood just north of downtown Asheville, our 2 bedroom / 1 bath basement suite w/ private entrance is within easy walking or quick driving distance of both downtown (1.5 miles) and the famous Grove Park Inn (1 mile).

The space
The space is a converted basement, formerly servants’ quarters, now has in-floor heating and updated EVERYTHING, but retains plenty of original character and charm. High ceilings and exposed brick help make this cool suite feel comfortable and cozy.

Note that our family with two young kids lives upstairs. We want you to have an excellent time, so if some walking above your head will disrupt your trip, consider this before you book. Additionally, while there’s walk out access in the back, this is a basement suite - we don’t want you to be surprised! Note that we do have occasional wildlife visitors of the black bear variety. They’re not considered dangerous, but we are respectful
neighborhood_overview: Stay close to local restaurants to meet your every need, from breakfasts at City Bakery, lunch at Taco Temple, and late dinners at Bone & Broth, Jettie Rae's, or Luella's BBQ. You can also hang out at Grove Park down the hill or in our backyard. Caution: the hammocks are very comfortable, so plan your afternoon accordingly.

name: 306 SW Condo Asheville - Historic Art Deco Gem!
description:
Stay in the historic SW Cafeteria Building! Built in 1929, the building is iconic art deco architecture, located in the center of downtown! The condo is spacious 1000 square feet with hard wood floors, exposed brick, and open light filled living/dining and kitchen. Highland Brewery taproom and high end food hall in commercial space on first floor and mezzanine. You can walk to everything downtown has to offer!

The space
306 SW Condo is located in one of Asheville's most treasured buildings, the S&W Cafeteria Building built in 1929 by premier art deco architect Douglas Ellington. The location is in the center of the city, with restaurants and the brewery district all within easy walking distance. This spacious condo has high end furnishings and features art work by local Asheville artists. The sofa pulls out to a very comfortable queen bed, with a memory foam mattress for extra guests.
host_about: My husband and I live in Asheville, North Carolina, and own and manage this lovely condo in the historic SW Cafeteria Building in downtown Asheville.  We manage our own property, and attend to every detail to make our guest stays  comfortable and accommodating to traveler needs.  We like to travel, and book properties that are short term rentals as well.  We enjoy hosting guests, as well as being a guest, and we always are respectful of properties,  We leave rental properties as if it is our own, and don't leave a mess for the cleaning staff.  We have two grown children.

description:
An elegant and well appointed tiny home with stainless steel appliances and a tiled shower, blue velvet couch and a comfy memory foam mattress up in the loft. Spacious and open with hardwood floors, this is a beautiful place for your retreat, business vacation, or sightseeing adventure.

The space

We are just outside of the city limits, about 15 minutes to downtown.

Guest access

Stroll the grounds of the Biltmore estate within 25 mins or enjoy a cocktail on the terrace of the historic grove park inn only 5 mins away. The river arts district and a plethora of breweries are 15 minutes from the front door. host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

host_about:
Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which, as you can guess, thrilled my parents to no end.  

Turns out, Asheville was the perfect place to be creative, get quiet, wake the heck up - and spend the next 15 years as a touring performing songwriter on my own record label. (Shared stages with everyone from The Beach Boys to John Mayer to Nanci Griffith - and made 7 CD's along the way.)

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

neighborhood_overview: The Cane Creek Valley is arguably one of the most beautiful areas in western NC. It is super convenient as a "base camp" from which to explore the many amenities the region has to offer, from the restaurants and shops of Asheville and Hendersonville, to the waterfalls of Brevard and trails off the Blue Ridge Parkway.  The 1.5 acre property where the apartment is located is level, open, and commands a view of Burney Mountain that changes with the seasons, the time of day,  and the weather. Rise early enough in the morning and you'll see the whisps of "smoke" and fog that give the Smoky Mountains their name. In the evening, experience the golden glow as the sun goes down, and enjoy a crackling fire from the comfort of Adirondack chairs.  It's easy, relaxed mountain living at its finest! We've lived here since 2005 and love life in the Smoky Mountains. It's great fun to introduce the lifestyle, sights, and amenities here to our clients and to the guests who stay in our "Cane Creek Valley Swim-Soak-Stay" guest quarters.

We have four adult children and four grandchildren spread out across the U.S., but our current "children" are our two sweet pups, Toby the Cairn Terrier (think Toto from the Wizard of Oz) and Greta the rescue pup, who form the "doggie welcoming committee."

description:
Looking for a place with the calm and quiet of a mountain cabin, yet 3.5 miles from downtown? Our house rests in a quiet mountain neighborhood on 1.3 acres of forest with views of the French Broad River and plenty of space to play and explore! Take a walk out the door down to the old barrel road next to the Om Sanctuary, from where you might spot the noon train. Upon your return, cool off with a drink on the balcony as deer, turkey vultures, and the occasional bear meander through the yard.

The space

It also captures the unique character of Asheville - a mix of mountain and industry - including the French Broad Chocolate Factory, a few breweries (Ginger's Revenge and Zilicoah), and an industrial supply company, to name a few.  At the bottom of our road is the French Broad Outfitters and river access for a variety of activities.  Richmond Hill Park is a few minutes drive and a bit longer walk from our house, which boasts trails and a disc golf course.  The Omni Grove Park Inn is a 10-minute drive away, and the Biltmore just a bit more at about 12-15 minutes.

host_about:
Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which, as you can guess, thrilled my parents to no end.  

Turns out, Asheville was the perfect place to be creative, get quiet, wake the heck up - and spend the next 15 years as a touring performing songwriter on my own record label. (Shared stages with everyone from The Beach Boys to John Mayer to Nanci Griffith - and made 7 CD's along the way.)

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

neighborhood_overview:
We are centrally located on the Greenway bike paths and 2 miles from the center of downtown. At most, we are a short Uber to all the local attractions.

For those who like to walk, the Asheville Adventure Center is right next door. Homegrown Restaurant and the Cascade Lounge are a short walk to the West.

12 Bones, the Wedge and the River Art Galleries are a short walk East. Following the bike path about a mile East lead to the amazing New Belgium Brewery Complex.
host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
When I am in the mountains I am home!  I've lived in the Piedmont region of NC for 14 years now but, Asheville will always be home.  I am on the struggle bus of being a mom to my two boys, Kelvin 4 and Brody 2. My night in shining armor, Ben loves coaching middle school football and teaching 8th grade math. 
I was raised by a single mother from Cleveland Ohio with strong beliefs and the loudest laugh in the south! She believed that the most important things in life are those that can never be taken away; education and experiences!  She is the fundamental reason I am a realist, yet fearless and ready to take on the world. Our yearly trips to NYC led to us sharing a love of the city and Broadway!

Of course Ben caught the travel bug too and has been back to NYC countless times! He's expanded to international travel! Last year it was a trip to Jamaica that led to my mom and I talking ourselves into seeing Hamilton before the original cast split up! She ended up backing out but of course Ben knows the number one mom lesson, "You don't regret what you do, only what you don't do." It was a priceless experience I wouldn't trade! 
I am proud to say my boys can tell you all about their trips to New York City(while singing Hamilton), New England and all the way down to Key West! Live your life, enjoy it,cars are designed to be driven, money is made to be spent - go make lasting memories!

host_about:
We are world travelers that love meeting people and experiencing new cultures, customs & foods. As frequent travelers, and parents of two young boys (with another on the way), we never found hotels ideal for our needs as they often lacked the local character we were looking for and rarely provided space families need. We loved staying at Airbnbs but unfortunately had some unpleasant experience due to hosts that didn't take pride in their homes and the experience they provided.

As entrepreneurs, we decided to solve the problem ourselves which is why we started hosting ourselves and eventually created Rabbu. Rabbu is a full-service boutique-home experience company that provides guests with a local and authentic, yet consistently comfortable accommodation experience whether it be for one day or multiple months.

Keeping true to our backgrounds, Rabbu is inclusive of all guests no matter race or background. In fact, we encourage diversity and many of the properties that we operate are purposefully in true and authentic neighborhoods that feature lots of diversity and character. It truly is the best way to experience a city.

All of our units allow for self check-in and are professionally cleaned, provide free WiFi, toiletries and premium sheets/linens to ensure that guests have a comfortable experience. Guests will enjoy a worry-free stay while also being immersed in the authentic culture of the cities and neighborhoods they are visiting through our carefully selected and decorated spaces. We have also partnered with local service providers and restaurants to provide our guests with discounts, offers, services and recommendations which only locals are typically privileged to.

We live by a simple motto: 'Treat Others How You Wish To Be Treated' and that is the core value we have built Rabbu around. We want our guests to experience a city how we as travelers want to experience.

Come experience our properties and truly feel a part of the community you are visiting.

neighborhood_overview:
The Montford Area Historic District is one of the prettiest neighborhoods in the country--though we're admittedly a little biased. Most of the neighborhood's residences were constructed between 1890 and 1920 in the Victorian or Queen Anne Victorian styles, though you'll also find architecture in the Arts and Crafts, Neoclassical, and Colonial Revival styles. Residents pride themselves on their gardening and landscaping expertise, benefited in no small part by the region's capacity for growing an incredible diversity of flora, from the signature magnolia trees, to flowering shrubs like the rhododendron & azalea, to bamboo, succulents, and so much more.

The gorgeous local cemetery is worth a visit, marking the final resting place of authors Thomas Wolfe and O. Henry. North Montford was once home to the Highland Hospital, in which Zelda Fitzgerald tragically died in a fire in 1948.

description:
This gorgeous house is located in the heart of Asheville, walking distance to Biltmore village and downtown AVL. Mission hospital is 5 minutes away.
host_about:

I love connecting with travelers and providing insight on the nuances of this vibrant city, while doing everything I can to make your stay in Asheville a phenomenal one. I'm always available via phone or the app and am happy to answer any and all questions you have!  

I love to cook and eat, so many of my recommendations revolve around food. I'm guessing if you are visiting Asheville for the first time you were probably drawn in by the food and/or beer scene, so we already have something in common! Best wishes, Christy

Welcome to the Sallie Lee Cottage! We hope you will enjoy your stay in Asheville in this charmingly renovated Historic Montford Cottage!

Proud to be a Victorian, the Sallie Lee Cottage is an exquisite example of the architectural wonders of the late 1800s. Furthermore, the interior is equally exceptional, centering around its unique triangular fireplace; which results a distinct Latin cross floor plan.

The home

Haw Creek valley’s southern boundary extends from US Highway 70/Tunnel Road at I-240 eastward along Tunnel Road to Maple Springs Road. description:
A short ten minute walk from this fabulous, kid-friendly two bedroom house that we call "Blue Dream" finds you in the heart of downtown Asheville. This 2 bed/1 bath home features an open concept downstairs living room/kitchen with an incredible "secret playhouse" under the stairs, a custom live-edge white oak dining table and a spacious and welcoming patio for outdoor entertaining.

The space
Walls of windows and a glass door invite you into this charming and eclectic space. The downstairs is an open concept living/dining area. There is a Roku Smart TV with cable, selection of boardgames, and a funky playhouse under the stairs.

The kitchen features soapstone countertops, a fully stocked kitchen with cooking basics (spices, oil) , a large fridge and freezer (with ice trays), coffee maker (with some starter coffee), tea kettle (with a small tea assortment), blender, toaster, a large custom live-edge white oak table and a spacious living area for lounging.
neighborhood_overview:
Our neighborhood is the charming Chestnut Hill Historical District of downtown Asheville. We are an easy 10 minute walk to the main area of downtown, a 12 minute drive to the Biltmore Estate, a 15 minute drive north for the Blue Ridge Parkway and Folk Art Center, a 15 minute drive to the NC Arboretum (Discount Shoes is on the way) and the BRP headed South to Mt Pisgah, a 10 minute drive to the River Arts District, a 5 minute drive to the breweries of the South Slope and 22 minute drive to the Asheville Regional Airport.
Our neighborhood itself has a couple of wonderful lunch cafés, three restaurants open for dinner only, the best butcher shop in town that has grab-and-go sandwiches, prepared meals and outrageous sausages and meats and of course we are only two blocks to Trader Joe's, Harris Teeter supermarkets and three blocks to Whole Foods.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

neighborhood_overview:
Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. neighborhood_overview: The small town of Woodfin, NC rests along the banks of the French Broad River and its convenient location next to I-26 makes for a quick 5-minute drive to downtown Asheville. host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

host_about:
Our family visited Asheville, NC, during one of our sightseeing tours across the United States, and we instantly fell in love with the city - so much so that we decided to purchase a vacation house there!  And the minute we stepped inside the Zurich Swiss Chalet property, we knew it was the one.

The Brown House is on a dead-end, one lane, private road. Our property sits under the Blue Ridge Parkway, a National Park, as it traverses High Swan, which is a 4340 foot high point. On up into the mountains is Mt. Mitchell, the highest spot in the eastern US. We have a few houses around with both a lot of open space and wooded areas. You might see cows and wild turkeys as you drive in. Maybe a bear or deer.

Riceville is the least developed quadrant of the immediate Asheville area. The Blue Ridge Parkway access is about four miles away, but it is actually much closer, just up on the side of High Swan.

On the one side of our property is a rural Work Exchange Community whereby people live on the land and work on it in exchange for their dwelling space. Often you can hear the sounds of children at play in the near distance.

In the early 1980s, ElizabethAnn decided to start a business downtown on Broadway Street & Futon designs came to life. That business, slightly ahead of its time, attracted travelers to inquire further about Asheville. There were two other women owned businesses in town at that time, Jewelry Design & Malaprops bookstore, both of which prosper today. neighborhood_overview:
Montford is an historic neighborhood in Asheville, North Carolina, located just north of downtown. A portion of Montford is a National Register Historic District with 600+ buildings, mostly residences built between 1890 and 1920. Few neighborhoods express the rich architectural heritage and vitality of Asheville better than the Montford Historic District.

Explore the 3.5 miles of roads through Riverside Cemetery, the final resting place for authors Thomas Wolfe and William Sydney Porter (better known as O. Henry) as well as North Carolina Governor Zebulon Vance, and 13,000 others.

The Montford Park Players, North Carolina's Longest Running Shakespeare Festival, presents free Theatre in the Park all summer long. The performances are held at the Hazel Robinson Amphitheater starting at 7:30 PM.

neighborhood_overview:
West Asheville is a hip and eclectic neighborhood with a downtown of its own. Best brunch contenders Sunny Point and Biscuit Head, the Admiral, New Belgium Brewery and many more are within walking or biking distance. Riverside park (has a dog park!) and Carrier park, hiking/biking and river floating are all just a hop and skip away. host_about:
My grandparents built this house in 1959. My grandfather was a Major General, head of the 13th AD, and a graduate of West Point in 1915, along with Eisenhower and Omar Bradley. After getting shot in WW2, his military career ended and he and my grandmother moved to Asheville so he could run the VA Hospital in Oteen. 

The house next door and three acres is what they bought in 1945 after witnessing a double rainbow over the mountains. After my mother and father moved us four kids to the upstairs of that house, my grandparents got an architect who studied with Frank Lloyd Wright to design the mid-century modern house next door, and my childhood was spent going between the houses. 

Four years ago I came up to renovate the place in order to sell it, but after watching a full moon rise over the mountains, I fell in love with it all over again and bought it. It's a comfort knowing this property has never left our family. I can feel all my relations here and enjoy the memories I had, mostly with my loving, brilliant, funny grandmother in this house. It has been a gathering spot for many famous people, including Ike and Mamie, who were close friends of my grandparents, and Carl Sandburg. 

I am an artistic welder and a singer and have travelled all over the world entertaining the troops for the Dept of Defense. Along the path of my travels, I always appreciated the kindness of locals who guided me when lost or recommended flavorful local places set apart from the tourist track. I'm here to offer you the same guidance.

There are sculptures and furniture inside and around my property that I made. 

 I love meeting new people, and I also love my privacy. I respect guests privacy as well and am available with any questions, concerns, interests you may have, but otherwise will not intrude. I live upstairs, and I am sensitive to being quiet. I encourage my guests to feel right at home. 

The expansive yard has plenty of areas to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee or a cocktail. The garden beds have herbs you are welcome to use.

Feel free to text with any questions prior to your stay as well as during your stay. My goal is for everyone who books the studio to enjoy the view, the birds, the wildlife, and the close proximity to everything fun while feeling far away, so much so, that they want to come back!!!

name: Sweet Suite
description:
We have a one bedroom, 1 bath suite in a quiet neighborhood conveniently located about 4 miles from downtown Asheville and from the Blue Ridge Parkway. Enjoy a private entrance and off street parking. The suite includes an efficiency kitchen. Licensed Home Stay Permit 15-16167.
Please note that AT&T phone service will not work in our neighborhood.

The space
The bedroom has a queen size bed with a new memory foam mattress. The living area has a full size futon that pulls out for sleeping. Kitchen includes coffee maker, mini fridge, toaster oven, induction burner, microwave oven..

Guest access
Basement apartment only.
